passage:
On my second month as a trainee at the architecture firm, I sent the site the wrong ceiling height for a classroom. Three hundred millimetres too low. I found it myself on a Friday evening, rechecking a drawing for something else.
Nobody else had noticed. The contractor would start the framing on Monday.
I sat in the empty office for twenty minutes, sweating. I could quietly send a "revised" drawing and hope nobody compared. But if the framing started wrong, children would sit in that room for years.
I called Lakshmi Ma'am, my supervisor, at home.
She was sharp. "How did this happen? Did you not check against the section?" I said no, I hadn't, and that it was my mistake. She was quiet, then: "Send the corrected drawing now, copy me. I'll call the contractor."
It stung for a week. But since then, she gives me the checking of other people's drawings.
Chaitanya

qa.q: How much too low was the ceiling height Chaitanya sent?
qa.a: The ceiling height was three hundred millimetres too low.

qa.q: What was Chaitanya feeling in the empty office?
qa.a: Chaitanya was frightened and sweating, tempted to fix it quietly, but worried about children sitting in a wrongly built room for years.

qa.q: Which choice made the difference, and what came of it?
qa.a: Calling Lakshmi Ma'am that evening and owning the mistake led to a scolding, but the error was fixed before building began, and Chaitanya was later trusted to check others' drawings.

qa.q: How might Lakshmi Ma'am see Chaitanya after this?
qa.a: Lakshmi Ma'am was angry at first but now seems to trust Chaitanya more, since someone who reports their own errors can be relied on to check others.

grounding: A trainee reports their own drawing error before it is found, faces a sharp scolding, and later earns more trust from the supervisor.

Course note, Physics Lab II. Written by Uday, faculty in charge, 18 February.
Tanvir, one of our final-year teaching assistants, came to my office at 8 a.m. today, before class. He looked as if he hadn't slept.
He told me that while grading the circuits quiz last night, he had used last year's answer key for the first twenty papers. Six students had lost marks they had earned. No student had complained yet; the marks were not published.
I was not gentle. I told him that grading is a trust we give assistants, and that he should have checked the key before starting. He did not argue or make excuses. He said, "You're right. I've already regraded all twenty with the correct key. The changes are in this sheet."
Next steps: marks published correctly this afternoon. I have told Tanvir that I will continue to give him grading duties. Frankly, I trust him more after this morning, not less.

qa.q: How many papers had Tanvir graded with last year's key?
qa.a: Tanvir had graded the first twenty papers with last year's key.

qa.q: What does Tanvir's look in the morning suggest he was feeling?
qa.a: Tanvir looked as if he had not slept, suggesting he was anxious and afraid of how Uday would react to the mistake.

qa.q: What did Tanvir do that turned a mistake into trust?
qa.a: He reported the error before anyone found it, accepted the scolding without excuses, and had already regraded all twenty papers.

qa.q: How might the six students have been affected if Tanvir had stayed silent?
qa.a: They would have lost marks they had earned, possibly without ever knowing why, and the course's fairness would have been harmed.

grounding: A faculty member records a student assistant who reports his own grading error before it is found, takes the scolding and earns greater trust.

subtype: Admitting a mistake at work or college [Actor]

Café manager's note, Saturday
At 3:40 pm Indu, our weekend trainee, came to me pale and said, "I wrote the wrong label on Mrs D'Souza's birthday cake. I wrote 'nut-free', but I used the almond sponge. The pickup is at five."
Nobody else had noticed. Abhinav, on the counter, had already boxed it.
I'll be honest: I scolded her. I said allergy labels are the one thing we can never get wrong. She nodded and didn't argue, though her hands were shaking.
Then we fixed it. I called Mrs D'Souza, explained, and offered a fresh nut-free cake by six or a full refund. Indu and I baked the new sponge together. It went out at 5:55.
What I did next: I added a second check for allergy labels on every order, and I told Indu that because she spoke up, nobody got hurt. From next month I'm putting her in charge of the allergy checklist.

qa.q: What did Indu write on the cake label?
qa.a: 'Nut-free', though the almond sponge was used.

qa.q: What do Indu's pale face and shaking hands suggest?
qa.a: They suggest Indu was frightened of the scolding and of what could have happened, yet chose to speak up anyway.

qa.q: What did the manager do after the scolding?
qa.a: Called Mrs D'Souza, baked a fresh nut-free cake with Indu, added a second allergy check, and planned to put Indu in charge of the allergy checklist.

qa.q: How might Mrs D'Souza feel about the call?
qa.a: Mrs D'Souza might be annoyed about the delay but relieved and grateful the error was caught before the birthday.

grounding: Shows a trainee reporting her own dangerous labelling error before anyone noticed, taking a scolding, and earning greater trust afterwards.

subtype: Admitting a mistake at work or college [Actor]
passage:
Monday
I told Pradeep sir today. My legs were jelly.
Last Friday, cleaning up the lab computer, I deleted a folder I thought was mine. It was his three weeks of plant growth readings. Nobody knew. The backup only runs on Sundays, so they'd have been gone.
I could have said nothing. He'd have blamed the old computer.
I went to his cabin at nine. "Sir, I deleted your readings folder on Friday by mistake."
He shouted. Properly shouted. "Do you know what three weeks means?" I stood there with my face burning.
Then he rubbed his eyes and said, "Fine. The lab assistant has a USB copy from Thursday. We'll lose one day, not three weeks. Next time, ask before deleting anything."
This evening he asked me to help him re-enter Friday's data. He said, "You told me before I found out. I'll remember that."
Damini

qa.q: What did Damini delete?
qa.a: Pradeep sir's folder of three weeks of plant growth readings.

qa.q: How did Damini feel going to Pradeep sir's cabin?
qa.a: Damini was terrified, legs like jelly, and felt a burning face during the scolding.

qa.q: Why did speaking up early turn out better than silence?
qa.a: They recovered the Thursday copy and lost only one day, and Pradeep sir now trusts Damini more for telling before being found out.

qa.q: How did Pradeep sir's feelings change during the day?
qa.a: He was furious at first, calmer once the USB copy turned up, and by evening appreciated that Damini told him first.

grounding: Shows a student reporting her own error before it was found, facing a scolding, and gaining more trust than silence would have protected.

subtype: Admitting a mistake at work or college [Actor]
passage:
The evening milk had been poured and the farmers had gone home when Ganga noticed it. In the register at the Rampur dairy collection centre she had written Shankar Kaka's cans as eight litres. The slip on the spike said eighteen.

Nobody would check before Saturday's payments. If anyone noticed later, she could blame the smudged slip.

Her fingers were cold. She carried the register to Sonali-didi, who was locking the cooling tank.

"Didi, I wrote eight instead of eighteen for Shankar Kaka. It's my mistake."

Sonali's voice rose so sharply that the helper boy looked over. "Do you know how that looks if he complains first? Twice you've been careless this month!"

Ganga stood and took it, face burning. They corrected the entry together, and Sonali signed beside it.

A month later, when Sonali went away for her sister's wedding, it was Ganga she left with the register and the keys.

qa.q: What did the slip on the spike say?
qa.a: The slip on the spike said eighteen.

qa.q: How did Ganga feel as she carried the register to Sonali?
qa.a: Ganga was scared, her fingers cold, yet determined to report her own mistake before anyone else found it.

qa.q: What went wrong, and what fixed it?
qa.a: Ganga made an entry error; reporting it at once and correcting it together, with Sonali's signature, fixed it before it could hurt Shankar Kaka's payment.

qa.q: How does Sonali's view of Ganga change by a month later?
qa.a: Though Sonali scolded her, she came to trust Ganga enough to leave her the register and the keys during the wedding.

grounding: Illustrates a young woman reporting her own error before it is found, facing a scolding, and earning more trust afterwards than silence would have protected.
